---
title: CI integration
description: Running email tests against the sandbox from a continuous-integration pipeline.
---

Use a **sandbox key** in CI. Sandbox mail never leaves the sandbox, so pipelines can run against real sign-up and reset flows safely.

<Steps>
<Step title="Store the key as a secret">
Add `TESTINBOX_API_KEY` to your CI provider's secret store. Never print it in logs.
</Step>
<Step title="Create inboxes per test">
```yaml title=".github/workflows/e2e.yml"
jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
        env:
          TESTINBOX_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.TESTINBOX_API_KEY }}
```
</Step>
<Step title="Tag inboxes by workflow">
Pass `tags: ["ci", "signup-flow"]` when creating inboxes so the dashboard groups them; see [Inbox lifecycle](../concepts/inbox-lifecycle#tags).
</Step>
</Steps>

## Webhooks instead of polling

For pipelines that fan out, register a [webhook](/api/webhooks/create-webhook) for `message.received` and let the delivery trigger the next job.

<Callout type="note">
Webhook secrets are shown once. Store them next to the API key.
</Callout>
